beats.text: Stonehenge, a prehistoric wonder on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, England, two miles (3 km) west of Amesbury.
beats.say: Stonehenge, a prehistoric wonder on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, England, two miles (3 km) west of Amesbury.

beats.text: Constructed in several phases, starting around 3100 BC and continuing until about 1600 BC.
beats.say: Constructed in several phases, starting around 3100 BC and continuing until about 1600 BC.

beats.text: The famous circle of large sarsen stones was placed between 2600 BC and 2400 BC.
beats.say: The famous circle of large sarsen stones was placed between 2600 BC and 2400 BC.

beats.text: Inside, a ring of smaller bluestones from Wales.
beats.say: Inside, a ring of smaller bluestones from Wales.

beats.text: Radiocarbon dating suggests the bluestones were placed between 2400 and 2200 BC.
beats.say: Radiocarbon dating suggests the bluestones were placed between 2400 and 2200 BC.

beats.text: Burials from as early as 3000 BC have been found within the site.
beats.say: Burials from as early as 3000 BC have been found within the site.

beats.text: Stonehenge is aligned towards the sunrise on the summer solstice, a feature unique among contemporary monuments.
beats.say: Stonehenge is aligned towards the sunrise on the summer solstice, a feature unique among contemporary monuments.

beats.text: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, Stonehenge is a British cultural icon, with a rich history spanning thousands of years.
